_note: What ARP wrote on chain for the skill catalogue. A RECORD, not a source of truth: every id here is a pure function of the URL or the word (ADR 0077, 0054), so the whole set is re-derivable with no credential and no network. What is not re-derivable is which ones ARP asserted, and which it later withdrew.
_authorisation: Signed by the agent session using AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY on the user's explicit instruction on 2026-10-29 (« je veut noté les skills », « on a cas creer toute les arrete necessaire », « oui il faut faire juste »). ADR 0037's three conditions: the key was never read into the agent's context, the signer address was checked against AGENT_ADDRESS before signing, and this file is the record. security.md scopes its automation prohibition to mainnet.
_unit: One row per SKILL, not per repository (ADR 0077). The URL is the install command's two arguments: `npx skills add <repo> --skill <name>`. `…#<name>` was rejected before anything was written — normaliseToolUrl drops the fragment, so 55 skills would have hashed to one atom.
_retired: 203 `has tag` positions were retired on 2026-10-29, not deleted — Intuition has no deletion. A keyword table ordered general before specific and `blockchain` matched `token` in 'cuts token usage' and in 'design tokens'. Redeeming the position removes the claim from ARP's index and leaves the triple on chain, unowned: ARP said it, then stopped. scripts/verify/audit-skill-tags.ts re-derives this and returns 0 disagreements.
_hashes: Absent for most writes, and that is a defect in the tooling rather than a choice. send-plan-in-waves.sh wrote each wave to a mktemp file and deleted it, so the hashes of 500+ writes were gone when the wave ended. Fixed the same day — it now appends them to <plan>.hashes.txt — but this run's are lost. The terms are re-derivable; a hash is not.
